## Proof

**Setup.** Let $\mathfrak c = |\mathbb R| = 2^{\aleph_0}$. Define the iterated power-set (beth) hierarchy above $\mathfrak c$:
$$\beth_0(\mathfrak c)=\mathfrak c,\qquad \beth_{n+1}(\mathfrak c)=2^{\beth_n(\mathfrak c)},\qquad \beth_\omega(\mathfrak c)=\sup_{n<\omega}\beth_n(\mathfrak c).$$

**Step 1 — Cardinality of each $V_n$.** We prove by induction that $|V_n|=\beth_n(\mathfrak c)$.

- Base: $V_0=\mathbb R$, so $|V_0|=\mathfrak c=\beth_0(\mathfrak c)$.
- Step: $V_{n+1}=V_n\cup\mathcal P(V_n)$. Since $|\mathcal P(V_n)|=2^{|V_n|}>|V_n|$ (Cantor), the union has cardinality $\max(|V_n|,2^{|V_n|})=2^{|V_n|}=\beth_{n+1}(\mathfrak c)$.

So $|V_n|=\beth_n(\mathfrak c)$ for every finite $n$.

**Step 2 — Cardinality of $\mathbb V$.** Since $\mathbb V=\bigcup_{n<\omega}V_n$ is a countable union,
$$|\mathbb V|\le\sum_{n<\omega}|V_n|\le\aleph_0\cdot\beth_\omega(\mathfrak c)=\beth_\omega(\mathfrak c).$$
Conversely $V_n\subseteq\mathbb V$ for every $n$, so $|V_n|\le|\mathbb V|$, giving $|\mathbb V|\ge\sup_n\beth_n(\mathfrak c)=\beth_\omega(\mathfrak c)$. Hence
$$|\mathbb V|=\beth_\omega(\mathfrak c).$$

**Step 3 — Cardinality of $\mathcal P_{fin}(\mathbb V)$.** Let $\kappa=|\mathbb V|=\beth_\omega(\mathfrak c)$, an infinite cardinal. The set of finite subsets decomposes by size:
$$\mathcal P_{fin}(\mathbb V)=\bigcup_{k<\omega}[\mathbb V]^k.$$
For each $k\ge 1$, $|[\mathbb V]^k|=\kappa^k=\kappa$ (cardinal arithmetic for infinite $\kappa$). Therefore
$$|\mathcal P_{fin}(\mathbb V)|\le\aleph_0\cdot\kappa=\kappa.$$
The reverse inequality $\kappa\le|\mathcal P_{fin}(\mathbb V)|$ holds via the injection $x\mapsto\{x\}$. Hence
$$|\mathcal P_{fin}(\mathbb V)|=\kappa=|\mathbb V|=\beth_\omega(\mathfrak c).$$

**Conclusion.**

$$\boxed{|\mathbb V|=|\mathcal P_{fin}(\mathbb V)|=\beth_\omega(\mathfrak c)=\sup_{n<\omega}\beth_n(\mathfrak c),\quad \beth_0(\mathfrak c)=|\mathbb R|,\ \beth_{n+1}(\mathfrak c)=2^{\beth_n(\mathfrak c)}.}$$

Both sets have the same cardinality, namely the $\omega$-th iterated power set of the continuum.

### PROOF COMPLETE
thinking:
The problem asks me to determine the cardinality of the superstructure V over R and its subset P_fin(V). Let me solve this directly.

V_0 = R, so |V_0| = c (continuum).
V_{n+1} = V_n ∪ P(V_n), so |V_{n+1}| = |P(V_n)| = 2^{|V_n|} (since power set dominates).

By induction, |V_n| = beth_n(c) where beth_0 = c, beth_{n+1} = 2^{beth_n}.

V = ∪_{n<ω} V_n, so |V| = sup_n beth_n(c) = beth_ω(c).

Now P_fin(V) = set of all finite subsets of V. For an infinite set of cardinality κ, |P_fin(κ)| = κ.

|P_fin(V)| = |V| = beth_ω(c).
